A reader-aware conversation viewport that follows streamed output at the live edge and releases control when the reader moves away.

What should the first release include?

Include streaming and recovery states too.
Yes. Those states make the first version feel dependable.

Keep results close to the action that produced them.

Pause the run, explain the impact, and ask before continuing.

Use the rail to jump between turns without losing your place.

Composition

Keep the scrolling viewport outside the message primitives it follows.

MessageScroller
└── MessageGroup
    └── Message
        └── MessageContent

Note: Message provides stable, semantic rows for the transcript. Prompt Input starts new turns without owning transcript movement. Streaming Response supplies the growing content the viewport follows.

How it works

A streaming transcript is not ordinary overflow. It must follow new output while the reader stays at the live edge, then stop moving the moment they choose to inspect earlier work.

Also on React Native. Follows new output and lets go when you scroll up.
Related components
Message

Composable conversation primitives for message rows, grouped bubbles, avatars, metadata, live markers, and a mount-only trailing-edge pop-up for newly sent rows.

Chat App

A complete agent conversation workspace composing navigation, messages, streaming, planning, approvals, tools, code, diffs, generated media, sources, and prompt input.

Tool Result

A lightweight execution disclosure for syntax-highlighted terminal output and request responses that collapses into a compact completed state.

About Message Scroller

Message Scroller is a React chat scroll container built for streaming AI responses. It follows new output while the reader sits at the bottom, stops following as soon as they scroll, swipe or press a key to read earlier messages, and resumes when they return to the live edge. An optional navigation rail lists the rendered messages as ticks with previews, highlights the one in view and scrolls to any message on click.

When to use it
An AI chat app streams long answers and readers need to scroll back without being pulled down.
A long agent transcript needs a compact rail to jump between earlier prompts and replies.
A support chat shows a "jump to latest" button when the reader is no longer at the bottom.
Accessibility

The viewport is a labeled section, and the content is a log role with a polite live region and aria-busy while you mark it busy, so screen readers hear new messages without interruption. Arrow Up, Page Up and Home, as well as wheel and touch, release following right away. Rail items have labels such as "Go to user message 2 of 6". With reduced motion enabled, following and rail navigation jump to position instead of scrolling smoothly.

FAQ
How do I auto scroll a chat to the bottom in React without trapping the reader?
Wrap your messages in MessageScroller. followOutput keeps it pinned while the reader is within followThreshold pixels of the end, and onFollowChange reports when they leave or return, for example to show a jump to latest button.
How do I add message navigation?
Set navigation to rail. The rail reads the rendered Message rows, builds previews from their text and appears once the transcript overflows. navigationLabel names it for screen readers.
Can I use it with the Vercel AI SDK?
Yes. It only manages the viewport. Render your useChat messages as children and set busy while a response is streaming.

How it works

A streaming transcript is not ordinary overflow. It must follow new output while the reader stays at the live edge, then stop moving the moment they choose to inspect earlier work.

Also on React Native. Follows new output and lets go when you scroll up.
Related components
Message

Composable conversation primitives for message rows, grouped bubbles, avatars, metadata, live markers, and a mount-only trailing-edge pop-up for newly sent rows.

Chat App

A complete agent conversation workspace composing navigation, messages, streaming, planning, approvals, tools, code, diffs, generated media, sources, and prompt input.

Tool Result

A lightweight execution disclosure for syntax-highlighted terminal output and request responses that collapses into a compact completed state.

About Message Scroller

Message Scroller is a React chat scroll container built for streaming AI responses. It follows new output while the reader sits at the bottom, stops following as soon as they scroll, swipe or press a key to read earlier messages, and resumes when they return to the live edge. An optional navigation rail lists the rendered messages as ticks with previews, highlights the one in view and scrolls to any message on click.

When to use it
An AI chat app streams long answers and readers need to scroll back without being pulled down.
A long agent transcript needs a compact rail to jump between earlier prompts and replies.
A support chat shows a "jump to latest" button when the reader is no longer at the bottom.
Accessibility

The viewport is a labeled section, and the content is a log role with a polite live region and aria-busy while you mark it busy, so screen readers hear new messages without interruption. Arrow Up, Page Up and Home, as well as wheel and touch, release following right away. Rail items have labels such as "Go to user message 2 of 6". With reduced motion enabled, following and rail navigation jump to position instead of scrolling smoothly.

FAQ
How do I auto scroll a chat to the bottom in React without trapping the reader?
Wrap your messages in MessageScroller. followOutput keeps it pinned while the reader is within followThreshold pixels of the end, and onFollowChange reports when they leave or return, for example to show a jump to latest button.
How do I add message navigation?
Set navigation to rail. The rail reads the rendered Message rows, builds previews from their text and appears once the transcript overflows. navigationLabel names it for screen readers.
Can I use it with the Vercel AI SDK?
Yes. It only manages the viewport. Render your useChat messages as children and set busy while a response is streaming.
